title: agctl status report, version 2
description: The document `agctl codex status --json` writes to stdout, and the shape a multi-provider report takes. Version 1 remains what `agctl claude status --json` emits and is not replaced by this. Like version 1, this document carries no token material: it is built from a row's identity, state and usage figures.

version.description: The report version. A consumer must refuse a version it does not know.

generated_at.description: When the report was built, RFC 3339 in UTC. Every countdown in the document is relative to this instant.

rows.description: The accounts the run displayed, in the order the table shows them. Rows hidden by default are present only when --all was given.

hidden.description: How many rows --all would have added. Zero when --all was given.

provider.description: Which vendor this row's usage came from. The same spelling the store's directories and the cache use.

id.description: The identifier --account accepts for this row.

kind.description: Where the credentials live and whether agctl may write them.

source.description: Where this row's credentials were read from, when the provider distinguishes that from the kind; null when it does not.

state.description: The row state as a stable, machine-readable token. New tokens may be added; a consumer must not assume the set is closed.

state_label.description: The same state as the sentence the table prints. Prose, and not stable across versions.

lock_state.description: What the namespace lock did on this pass.

note.description: The short explanation the table appends to the state, when there is one.

windows.description: Every usage window the response described, in the order it described them. A window's meaning comes from its kind and its label, never from its position here.

next_reset.description: The soonest reset across every window, RFC 3339 in UTC.

session_reset.description: When the five-hour session window rolls over, RFC 3339 in UTC.

weekly_reset.description: When the seven-day all-models window rolls over, RFC 3339 in UTC.

identity.description: Who the row is, in terms both providers can answer: which person, and which workspace of theirs. A consumer that needs Anthropic's own spelling for a Claude row has version 1.

user_id.description: The Anthropic account UUID, or the ChatGPT user id. Empty when the row has no identity.

account_id.description: The Anthropic organization UUID, or the ChatGPT account id.

plan_type.description: The subscription tier, as the credential or the response spelled it.

email.description: The account's email address, when it is known.

org_name.description: The organization's display name, when the provider has one.

kind.description: Which window this is. `unknown` is not an error: a window this build has never seen is still reported, with its kind string in the label.

label.description: The window's display label, which is where a scoped window's scope and an unrecognised window's raw kind string appear.

percent.description: The percentage the server sent, clamped to 0..=100.

percent_floor.description: The same figure floored, which is what the table and the vendors' own interfaces show.

resets_at.description: When the window rolls over, RFC 3339 in UTC.

is_active.description: Whether this is the window currently constraining the account.

limit_name.description: The vendor's own name for the limit, when it sent one. Null for every Claude window.

metered_feature.description: Which metered feature the window covers, when the vendor said.

normal_model_slug.description: The model slug the window's ordinary requests are billed as, when the vendor said.

credits.description: What is known about paid usage beyond the subscription. Tagged by `kind`, with every member present whatever the tag, so a consumer testing one gets an answer rather than having to tell an absent member from a null one.

kind.description: `money` when the vendor reports minor units and a currency, `balance` when it reports a decimal amount, `off` when credits are switched off, `unavailable` when the response said nothing about them — which is not the same as switched off.

used_minor.description: The amount spent, in minor units of `currency`. Only under `kind: money`.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code the minor units are in.

exponent.description: How many decimal places a minor unit represents.

limit_minor.description: The monthly ceiling in minor units, absent for an uncapped account.

percent.description: The server's own utilisation percentage, rounded.

balance.description: The balance exactly as the wire spelled it, digits and all. A string rather than a number because the response sends one, and a decimal amount of money that has been through a binary float is no longer the amount that was sent. Only under `kind: balance`.

unlimited.description: Whether the plan's balance is uncapped.

disabled_reason.description: Why credits are switched off, when the server said.

scope.description: Whose figures these are. `organization` means two rows of one organization report the same number, and a consumer that summed them would double-count.
